A 65-year-old man presents to the emergency department for evaluation of left arm and leg weakness.
He was walking in the park about 45 minutes prior to arrival when the patient stumbled and fell.
A non-contrast CT scan of the head is performed, which suggests parenchymal ischemia in the distribution of the right middle cerebral artery.
On exam, he has 3/5 strength in the left upper and lower extremities and a left-sided facial droop.
He is given intravenous alteplase with rapid improvement in his strength deficits and facial asymmetry.
